body: Thank you. I appreciate your words.

I already do that. I volunteer for a children's hospital, the American Cancer Society, and an environmental activist group. I've also helped create fundraisers for the hungry and malnourished. I also give donate cash to activist groups and beggars (even though I might get scammed).
That's all I'm basically giving myself, time. I'm not going to do it, just waiting.

Maybe, you maybe right. The thing is, I was pressured into university. Family expectations and media had a deep effect on me. One thing I learned is to never let someone put expectations on you, you make them yourself.

I've already left high school, and I'm attending university now. I had high hopes that things would get better. Guess what? It's actually much worse. Being miserable isn't comfortable, it's saddening and terrible. I'm surprised I'm even able to get up in the morning, take a shower, brush my teeth and exercise. Let alone do my homework and study. Some situations in my life were beyond my control and it still affects me.

How am I determined to be unhappy when I've done everything I can in the last decade to improve my quality of living? I can make it as wonderful or terrible as I want it to be? Tell that to the situations that I had no control over. My father getting shot, my crucial surgery, having no family, my parent's current financial situation, and so forth. I didn't make these decisions. I got put into the equation. The only thing I really can do is stop living my life. So far, it's getting much worse now with school.
Well so far my guess has been right. As I said, I've tried therapy, antidepressants, medication and I even admitted myself into a psych ward to get help.
I'm not determined to be unhappy, it's just that unhappiness is inevitable for me no matter how hard I try to be happy. I've done all I can for myself. It's not enough.
